subject: Mythology
title: The Cyclops: One-Eyed Monsters
description: A 60-second lesson on The Cyclops: One-Eyed Monsters.

hook.text: Polyphemus was a Cyclops who trapped Odysseus in his cave and ate two of his men for dinner every night.

buildup.text: Cyclopes were giant one-eyed beings. Some were savage shepherds; others were master craftsmen who forged divine weapons.

discovery.text: Odysseus escaped by blinding Polyphemus with a burning stake and hiding under sheep as they left the cave.

twist.text: Cyclops myths may come from ancient elephant skulls found in Greece. The nasal cavity looks like one giant eye socket.

climax.text: The Cyclopes forged Zeus's thunderbolt, Poseidon's trident, and Hades's helmet — the weapons that won the cosmic war.

punchline.text: The gods owe their thrones to one-eyed smiths and an elephant skull mix-up.

quiz.question: What may have inspired the one-eyed Cyclops myth?
options: Solar eclipse observations by ancient astronomers
Ancient elephant skulls whose nasal cavity resembles a single eye socket
People born with a rare medical condition
